_comment: THE ROUTING DENOMINATOR, FROZEN. Row e2099400 / d8d019f6; frozen 2026-08-26 on Maria's review finding.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. v2_eval's load_mappable_commands used to import load_v1_class_to_command from
v1_eval_arm, which reads the LIVE v1 registry out of the pinned worktree. That worktree and that
script are being deleted. The import runs on EVERY v2 eval, not only paired ones, and its failure
path returned None -- which makes routing accuracy score over the FULL corpus instead of the
eligible-only set, announced on stdout and nowhere else. Every number after the deletion would have
been silently incomparable to every number before it.
WHAT IT IS. The commands the v1 registry at pin sha 15536409 could route, which is the denominator
both arms score on. It is a CONSTANT, not a lookup: the pin is a fixed sha, so reading it live was
never buying freshness -- only a dependency.
HOW IT WAS GENERATED, and it is reproducible while the worktree still exists:
LUPIN_ROOT=<pinned-worktree> PYTHONPATH=src python -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src/scripts')
from v1_eval_arm import load_v1_class_to_command
print(sorted(set(load_v1_class_to_command()[0].values())))"
MEASURED BOTH WAYS, because the fork map is flag-dependent: with the pinned tree's own v2 registry
and with the main tree's, the class map has 7 entries and the COMMAND set is identical. CRUD forks
add class NAMES pointing at the same command (merge_fork_map ADDS, never RE-POINTS), so they cannot
change this list -- which is why freezing the commands is safe where freezing the classes would not be.
IF THIS FILE IS MISSING OR UNREADABLE, v2_eval RAISES. It does not fall back to the full corpus:
a wider denominator that still prints a percentage is the exact defect this replaces.
